newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea launches graft probes of top officials.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea launches graft probes of top officials.

text.p: South Korean authorities are investigating about 70 high-level government officials for alleged corruption, a presidential official said on Wednesday.

The official, who declined to be identified, provided no further details, but local media reported that the probe covered several cabinet ministers, vice-ministers and heads of local governments and wrongdoing by some had been detected.
South Korea has long been plagued by graft at the highest level, with two former presidents, Chun Doo Hwan and Roh Tae-woo, in jail for graft, treason and mutiny.
On Saturday President Kim Young-sam's second son, Kim Hyun-chul, was arrested on charges of accepting kickbacks worth millions of dollars and evading taxes.
That arrest followed a prosecution inquiry into corruption among politicians, government officials and bankers following the collapse of Hanbo Steel Co in January.

Opposition parties have alleged that Hanbo founder Chung Tae-soo helped bankroll the president's election win, and that Kim Hyun-chul laundered huge sums of leftover funds through his business cronies.
President Kim is widely expected to apologise over his son's arrest and address allegations of foul play linked to his 1992 election campaign.
But an aide at the presidential Blue House ruled out any statement on Wednesday, and said it was not clear whether any apology would be forthcoming.
"He will be making no statement today, and I cannot confirm any plans for an apology," said the official, who declined to be identified.
The Chosun Ilbo, South Korea's leading newspaper, said on Wednesday some of Kim's aides had questioned the need for an apology.
"Even if he 'confesses' he will not be able to reveal the whole truth, which will lead to continuous pressure from the opposition and the people to reveal everything," the paper said.

The latest probe was revealed at a meeting called by a senior presidential secretary on Wednesday to discuss ways to boost civil servants' morale after Hanbo and prevent corruption ahead of December's presidential polls, the official said.

Separately, Chief Prosecutor Shim Je-ryoon told reporters Kim Hyun-chul was questioned on Wednesday along with former top intelligence official Kim Ki-sup and two close associates of Hyun-chul, Park Tae-joong and Lee Sung-ho.
Kim Ki-sup, Park and Lee have been implicated in the graft scandal surrounding Hyun-chul.
Shim said the president's son was more cooperative on Wednesday than in the past and showed some signs of remorse.
